1.pericope_label: Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain; so the LORD shall make bright clouds, and give them showers of rain
debates: Whether the call to ask is a real command or a way of saying God is willing
Whether the idolatry reproved belongs to the prophet own day or to the past
Whether the bright clouds are clouds or lightnings
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch rejects the reading that makes the summons a mere figure of speech
Calvin finds an implied reproof in an exhortation that looks like plain encouragement
Ellicott defends the late date of the passage by arguing that idolatry outlasted the exile
themes: A promise that still has to be asked for
Rain sought from the clouds instead of from their maker
Two rains a year and nothing in between
Images believed to be built so as to talk back

3.pericope_label: Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the goats: for the LORD of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah
debates: Whether the shepherds are the nation own rulers or foreign oppressors
Whether the four things come out of God or out of Judah
Whether the mighty men are a historical army or the church
outliers: Ellicott identifies the goats with the shepherds and makes both foreign, against the other four voices
Ellicott corrects two tenses, so that the anger is present and the punishment still to come
Wesley reads the last of the four as a collector of tribute, and turns the reversal into the point
themes: Priests who are shepherds by office and goats by life
A stone that is ornament and support at once
A tent-peg holding the ropes that hold the tent
A quarrel that renews the love rather than weakening it

6.pericope_label: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them
debates: Whether the gathering call is a soft pipe or a shrill cry
Whether sowing among the nations means a fresh dispersion
Whether the promise of further redemption dates these chapters before the exile
outliers: Gill and Clarke render the same verb at opposite ends of the scale, a shepherd whistle and a shriek
Ellicott answers the dating objection by pointing to how few actually came back at the first return
Ellicott insists the verb rendered sow never carries the bad sense of scattering
themes: A call soft enough to be a reed and strong enough to carry
A restoration that left most of the people where they were
Seed sown rather than seed scattered
Men who turn back because they remembered

10.pericope_label: I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon
debates: Who or what passes through the sea
Whether the sea with affliction is a sea of affliction or a sea where affliction is
Whether the Lord in whom they are strengthened is the speaker or another
outliers: Gill sets out four subjects for the verb and declines to choose between them
Ellicott settles the subject as God and disputes only the construction of the phrase that follows
Clarke supports a messianic reading of the last verse from a paraphrase that reads by the Word of the Lord
themes: A land too small for the people coming back to it
Waters thrown from side to side until everyone is across
Neighbours glad to let go of people they profit by
One fold with no difference made inside it
